assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators opened a new classification of quantum matter based on band topology and protected boundary states. The Z2 invariant, the quantum spin Hall prediction and its realisation in HgTe wells are conceptually clear, original and have reshaped condensed matter physics, with spillover into spintronics, photonics and quantum materials.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the Z2 theory; Molenkamp's group delivered the decisive quantum spin Hall transport experiment (with Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang's HgTe prediction not in the credited set). Hasan's three-dimensional ARPES work is a further claim. Kane, Mele and Molenkamp form a defensible theory-plus-experiment trio, but the omitted names are a real attribution problem.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent materials, transport and ARPES studies over about two decades; interpretation is stable and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe prediction (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang) and for the three-dimensional topological insulator discovery (Hasan, Moore, Balents, Fu-Kane-Mele) is split and may not fit three names.
I rely on my own knowledge of the literature and have not verified priority details independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise clean, tunable many-body Hamiltonians, from the Mott-insulator transition to quantum gas microscopy. This is a statistical-physics laboratory in which interacting, disordered and out-of-equilibrium problems can be controlled and observed directly, with lasting impact across condensed matter and quantum information.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac and Gardiner) proposed the Hubbard-model realisation; Greiner and Bloch (with Hansch) demonstrated the superfluid-Mott transition, and Bloch developed quantum-gas microscopy and many-body simulation. Cirac is also credited and could replace a name, but Bloch, Greiner and Zoller give the clearest theory-experiment split. Jaksch and Hansch are not in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of independent replication across many groups; the platform is mature and has produced benchmark simulations, although the biggest scientific payoffs continue to arrive.
uncertainties: Overlap with the Cirac-Zoller trapped-ion and Rydberg candidates may favour a single combined quantum-simulation award and complicates credit.
Quantum-gas-microscope credit (Greiner, Bakr, Bloch, Kuhr and others) is spread over more people than the allowed three.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fluctuation theorems and the Jarzynski equality extend thermodynamics to small, driven, far-from-equilibrium systems and give exact relations between work, free energy and entropy production. They are a conceptual advance in nonequilibrium statistical physics with broad use in single-molecule biophysics and stochastic thermodynamics.
assessment.attribution: Evans, Cohen and Morriss (with Gallavotti, Searles and Kurchan) established the steady-state fluctuation theorem, Jarzynski derived the free-energy relation, and Crooks the detailed fluctuation theorem. Jarzynski and Evans are the clearest pair among the credited names, but Gallavotti, Cohen, Kurchan, Searles and Crooks all hold priority claims, so credit is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Verified experimentally in RNA-hairpin pulling, colloidal and electronic systems; the theory is stable, though recognition by physics prize standards is partly a question of attribution rather than evidence.
uncertainties: Priority is contested among at least five or six people, so a clean prize configuration is hard.
Experimental tests are largely mesoscopic and biophysical, so the committee may weigh breadth of physical consequence differently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene gave a flat-band platform with correlated insulators, superconductivity and later topological states, creating the field of moire quantum materials. The theoretical flat-band prediction and experimental discovery are clear and strongly original.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle and flat bands; Jarillo-Herrero's group reported the correlated insulator and superconductivity in 2018, with Cao as lead author (not credited). The theory plus experiment trio is clean given the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced by many groups and extended to other moire systems, but the origin of the superconductivity is still debated and the field is young; timing is somewhat early.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism and the full phase diagram remain debated.
Early-career contributors, notably Yuan Cao, are not in the credited set.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory gave the first controlled, non-perturbative framework for the Mott transition and strongly correlated electrons, based on the infinite-dimension limit. Combined with ab initio methods (DFT plus DMFT) it is a standard tool and the idea is an elegant statistical-physics mean-field construction.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimensional limit, Georges and Kotliar mapped the problem onto a quantum impurity model, and Müller-Hartmann and Jarrell also contributed. Vollhardt, Georges and Kotliar are a plausible trio but Metzner (not credited) is an important omission.
assessment.maturity: Established for about 30 years with many independent applications and extensions, though its role is as a method and the discovery is less a single observation.
uncertainties: Impact is methodological, which the committee may read as less decisive than a discovery.
Metzner's role and the roles of Müller-Hartmann, Jarrell and Rozenberg complicate allocation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cosmic inflation explains the flatness and horizon problems and the origin of primordial fluctuations, and its quantitative predictions for a near scale-invariant spectrum have been strongly supported by CMB and large-scale structure data. It is a deep, original idea in fundamental physics.
assessment.attribution: Guth proposed inflation, Linde (and Albrecht-Steinhardt) fixed the graceful exit problem, and Mukhanov (with Chibisov) computed the fluctuation spectrum. Starobinsky, whose earlier model is central, is absent from the credited names, and so is Sato; the allocation is a serious difficulty.
assessment.maturity: The spectrum predictions are supported, but the inflationary mechanism itself lacks a decisive test such as primordial B-modes, so I regard recognition as premature.
uncertainties: Primordial gravitational waves have not been detected, so the inflation hypothesis is not uniquely confirmed.
Starobinsky's priority claim is not representable in the credited names, and alternatives to inflation are not fully excluded.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of high-temperature superconductivity in iron pnictides and chalcogenides opened a second family of unconventional high-Tc materials, with distinct multiband physics and pairing symmetry. The finding is clear and has driven large experimental and theoretical activity.
assessment.attribution: Hosono's group discovered superconductivity in LaFeAsO(F) and then raised the Tc, which is the decisive experimental step; Mazin proposed s-plus-minus pairing, one of several contributors to the theory (with Kuroki, Hirschfeld and others). Hosono alone would be the cleaner configuration, and Mazin's addition is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced worldwide since 2008, with materials now well characterised, but the pairing mechanism remains unresolved and there is no application payoff yet comparable to cuprates.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism and symmetry are still debated.
Theory credit is spread (Mazin, Kuroki, Hirschfeld, Chubukov) and no single person is decisive.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics established strong coupling of superconducting qubits to microwave resonators and is the architecture underlying superconducting quantum processors. It is a key enabling advance with broad use in quantum information and quantum-limited measurement.
assessment.attribution: Blais (with Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf) wrote the theory proposal; Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling in 2004. Girvin is not credited; the theory and experiment division is clean otherwise.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed and widely adopted, though recognition may be tempered by the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum effects in superconducting circuits, and the platform's final significance is still developing.
uncertainties: Overlap with the recently recognised superconducting circuit work could reduce priority.
Girvin's and others' credit for the theory is not represented.
